title: feat(types): App/Dashboard/Page twins take the spec by reference, like their zod mirrors
body:
Fixes #9736

Clause-②: yes

Executes ruling `5732099575` (batch #167 item 4, letter 甲; the maintainer agreed with 「其他同意」 at 2026-09-18T15:17Z). The three hand-written TypeScript twins now take the spec by reference, the same way their zod mirrors do. The exclusion list is hoisted to one `as const` array. The mirror's `specFieldsExcept` call and the twin both read that array. This is a types-only change: no runtime code changes and no mirror is narrowed.

## What changed

| twin | extends | twin-only omission |
|---|---|---|
| `AppComponentSchema` (`app.ts`) | `BaseSchema`, plus Omit over spec `App` of `(typeof APP_SPEC_EXCLUDED)[number]` | none |
| `DashboardComponentSchema` (`complex.ts`) | `BaseSchema`, plus Omit over spec `Dashboard` of `DASHBOARD_SPEC_EXCLUDED` plus `'header'` | `header` |
| `PageNodeSchema` (`layout.ts`) | `BaseSchema`, plus Omit over spec `Page` of `PAGE_SPEC_EXCLUDED` plus `'slots'` plus `'assignedProfiles'` | `slots`, `assignedProfiles` |

- **Hoist only.** In `zod/{app,complex,layout}.zod.ts`, each inline list became `export const X_SPEC_EXCLUDED = [...] as const`, and `specFieldsExcept` now reads that array. The members are byte-identical, so the mirror's accept set does not change. The arrays are not re-exported from `zod/index.zod.ts`, which uses named re-exports. The twins read them with `import type`. `zod-mirror-parity`'s closed-population census now lists them in `EXCLUSIONS`, because they are key-name tuples, not schemas.
- **Twin-only omissions.** Only the compiler's collisions are omitted, and each one has a docblock line saying why. Dashboard `header` and Page `slots` are hand-written members that are **not assignable** to the spec's member. For `header`, `actionUrl` is optional where the spec requires it, `label` is `string` against `I18nLabel`, and `actionType` is an open string. For `slots`, `SchemaNode` admits `null` and primitives. Both are already ledgered in `KnownDrift` and `WiderThanDeclared`. Both are withheld on the type side only, and neither twin member was widened. The other twin-declared members (`icon`, `branding`, `active`, `hidden`, `requiredPermissions`, and the page's `object`, `template`, `variables`, `isDefault`, `aria`, `kind`) are assignable to the spec's member, so they override it without an omission. Page `assignedProfiles` is withheld the same way, for forward compatibility: objectstack `main` retires it (`retiredKey`), so the hand-written `string[]`, left unchanged, would fail the extends clause under the Spec Main Shape Gate. Its retirement is objectui#9409 (on hold). *(Added by the PM seat after commit `8e11943`.)*
- **`contextSelectors`** is in `APP_SPEC_EXCLUDED` because the mirror re-adds it with its own element. The ruling names it among the admitted keys, so the App twin now declares `contextSelectors` as an optional array whose element is the `z.input` of the mirror's `AppContextSelectorSchema`. That takes the mirror's own element by reference, and the generic is spelled out in words here because GitHub strips angle-bracket shapes. Without that declaration the App row could not reach zero.
- **Ledger.** The `MirroredUndeclared` rows for `app.zod.ts#AppComponentSchema` (20 keys), `complex.zod.ts#DashboardComponentSchema` (11) and `layout.zod.ts#PageNodeSchema` (10) are deleted. Each deletion leaves a note where its row stood. `assertionMirroredUndeclaredMatchesLedger` and `assertionMirroredUndeclaredRecordsEveryKey` still reconcile every pair, and the census sentence moves to the derived figures. No other ledger (`KnownDrift` / `UnmirroredDeclared` / `WiderThanDeclared`) moved.
- **Pins.** `twins-spec-by-reference-9736.test.ts`:
  - For each twin, the set of spec keys minus declared keys is `never`, with lit and negative controls.
  - Admitted keys have the spec's own member type. This is checked with `Equal`, not by assignment, because `BaseSchema`'s index signature would make an assignment vacuous.
  - `@ts-expect-error` on the tombstones App `version` and Dashboard `refreshInterval`, plus the mirror's parse refusal on the same literal.
  - The `header` and `slots` members keep their own types.
- `dashboard-aria-retired-contract-twins.test.ts` was rewritten. It pinned that `aria` is *not declared*. After this change `aria` is declared, but only as the spec tombstone typed `undefined`. The pin now asserts that, and it adds the `@ts-expect-error` that its old header said could not stick.

## Measured deviations from the dispatch's assumptions

- Tombstones surface as `?: undefined` (the `z.input` of `z.never().optional()`), not as `?: never`. For the accept set under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: false` they are equivalent: authoring a value is a compile error.
- On `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0, `Page` carries **no** tombstone. The Page pin therefore covers the admitted half only, and the test says so.

## Evidence

All readings below were taken on the merged head `a1cc88e32`, except where a line says otherwise. The consumer type-check, the reverse verification and the check scripts ran on the pre-merge head `1d24a9ef9` plus the changeset commit. The merge brought in only the `objectql*` files from sibling work, and the `@object-ui/types` type-check and vitest were re-run after it.

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` exited 0. It chains `tsc --noEmit`, then `tsconfig.examples.json`, then `tsconfig.test.json`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/ apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` reported 215 files and 5126 tests passed, exit 0, on the merged head.
- Consumer type-check (the downstream direction: every package whose source names one of the three interfaces) passed for all 10 packages: app-shell, components, core, layout, plugin-dashboard, plugin-designer, plugin-list, react, runner and example-schema-catalog. **Zero consumer fixes were needed.** This ran after a turbo build of their dependency closure (32 tasks).
- Reverse verification that consumers read the rebuilt `.d.ts`: a probe file in `plugin-dashboard/src` authored `refreshInterval: 5` on a `DashboardComponentSchema`. `tsc` went red with `TS2322 Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'undefined'`. The probe was then removed and `git status` was clean.
- eslint on the 9 changed `.ts` files: 0 errors. The 14 warnings are all pre-existing `no-explicit-any` hits on lines this diff does not touch.
- `check-changeset-presence`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:control-bytes`, `check:installed-pin-claims`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:published-dist`, `check:unreferenced-sources` and `check:published-tsconfig-exclude` all exited 0.

## Changeset: minor

`.changeset/9736-twins-spec-by-reference.md` declares `@object-ui/types` as `minor`. The published type surface gains members. One authoring spelling (a tombstone key) moves from a parse-time refusal to a compile-time refusal, and this repo marks breaking semantics `minor`, never `major`.

## Acceptance notes

- `check:changeset-claims` (report-only) lists 39 pending changesets that name files this diff touches. One of them now reads false: `.changeset/dashboard-aria-member-retired-5830.md` says `BaseSchema`'s index signature means an existing `aria:` line still compiles. After this PR it does not compile. That text is another change's pending declaration and is left untouched here. This PR's changeset states the new behaviour explicitly. Carrier: the release seat, or whoever next edits that changeset.
- Serial siblings objectui#10084 and objectui#10066 and PR objectui#10260 touch disjoint files. `origin/main` was merged before this PR opened, and the gates above re-ran on the merged head.
